[[File:Theodor Reye.jpeg|thumb|Theodor Reye]]
'''Karl Theodor Reye''' (born 20 June 1838 in [[Cuxhaven|Ritzebüttel]], [[Germany]] and died 2 July 1919 in [[Würzburg]], [[Germany]]) was a [[Germans|German]] [[mathematician]].  He contributed to geometry, particularly [[projective geometry]] and [[synthetic geometry]]. He is best known for his introduction of [[Configuration (geometry)|configurations]] in the second edition of his book, ''Geometrie der Lage'' (Geometry of Position, 1876).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Scott, Charlotte Angas|authorlink=Charlotte Scott|title=Reye's ''Geometrie der Lage''|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1899|volume=5|issue=4|pages=175–181|url=http://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1899-05-04/S0002-9904-1899-00580-9/|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1899-00580-9|doi-access=free}}</ref> The [[Reye configuration]] of 12 points, 12 planes, and 16 lines is named after him.

Reye also developed a novel solution to the following three-dimensional extension of the [[problem of Apollonius]]:  Construct all possible spheres that are simultaneously tangent to four given spheres.<ref>{{cite book| author = Reye T| year = 1879| title = Synthetische Geometrie der Kugeln| publisher = B. G. Teubner| location = Leipzig| url = http://www.gutenberg.org/files/17153/17153-pdf.pdf|language=de}}</ref>

==Life==

Reye obtained his Ph.D. from the [[University of Göttingen]] in 1861.  His dissertation was entitled "Die mechanische Wärme-Theorie und das Spannungsgesetz der Gase" (The mechanical theory of heat and the potential law of gases).

==Mathematical work==

Reye worked on [[conic section]]s, [[quadric]]s and [[projective geometry]].

Reye's work on linear manifolds of projective plane pencils and of bundles on spheres influenced later work by [[Corrado Segre]] on manifolds. He introduced [[Reye congruence]]s, the earliest examples of [[Enriques surface]]s.
